summary: Tested smart-routing (POST /teams/{id}/start), sticky direct chat with switch-agent, group smart_expand, and updated /messages response. Backend: 47/47 pytest pass (13 NEW in test_smart_routing.py + 19 agents catalogue + 15 soulprint). Frontend E2E: smart-start composer routed React perf question to Engineering · Frontend Developer (toast 'Routed to Frontend Developer'); switch-agent dialog handed off to marketing-content-creator with meta strip updating to 'CONTENT CREATOR · MARKETING'; new-conv dialog hides smart-expand-toggle on direct, shows it default-ON on group.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1014 lines — earlier suggestion to split (auth/orgs/teams/conversations/agents/router) is now more pressing. route_best_agent + should_expand_group + smart_start + switch_agent could live in a /app/backend/router.py module.

route_best_agent and should_expand_group both build a full _agent_menu (169 entries) on every call — fine functionally, but each routing call ships ~20KB of context to the LLM. Could be optimised by pre-trimming to one-line-per-agent (already done) or by clustering at the division level first, then refining within division.

switch_agent uses the user's own message slot for the bridging note. Pragmatic, but UX-wise the bridging text shows up as if the human typed it. Consider sender_type='system' for the bridging line to make the handoff visually distinct.

should_expand_group: parsing 'none' via .split()[:2] is robust against leading whitespace but will miss 'No expansion needed' phrasing. Tightening the system prompt to the literal `none` is fine; tested green.

Smart-start endpoint creates a conversation BEFORE the LLM reply succeeds; if generate_agent_reply fails, the conversation row exists but the agent_message DB row may not be created. Consider wrapping in a try/except that also writes a fallback agent message or rolls back the conversation.
